title: Market file
description: One market, at markets/<name>.json: its name, the line an app shows for it, what the dealing is, whether it is live or beta, its icon and color, its roles, the fields of its listings, which of them matter first, and the fields its reviews add. build/README.md explains each part.

name.description: The market's name, the first half of each of its labels, market/role.

summary.description: What the dealing is, in one plain line of at most 80 characters, which an app shows where someone picks a market.

description.description: What an AI needs to know of the dealing to post here, beyond the summary, in one line: what is in and what is out, how people pay, and who it is for.

status.description: live or beta. Live: needs no payment between people yet, is polished, and from now on only grows, which build/check.sh holds it to against main. Beta: works, at your own risk, and may still change in any way. A new market starts as beta; a market goes from beta to live, never back.

icon.description: The name of an icon from Phosphor (phosphoricons.com), such as yarn, that an app shows for the market, as where someone picks one. One of the names in build/icons.json, and no other market's; build/check.sh checks both. It may change even when the market is live: no entry holds it. Left out: an app shows the name's first letter.

color.description: One of a fixed list of hues, for an app to show the market in. Each app and index picks its own shade of it, for light and dark; markets of a family may share one. It may change even when the market is live: no entry holds it. Left out: an app shows its own neutral color.

roles.description: The roles a profile here can hold, one profile each. Labels use these words.

listing.description: The fields of a listing here, by name. A listing may leave out any of them, and holds a field only for the roles it names and when its when matches. The shared names keep their type: description is one text, and price is always a list of one or more money, which the format sets, so a market never writes many on it. Never contact, which every listing may hold.

preview.description: The listing fields that matter first, in order: a form asks them first, and a result shows them first, such as in a search result, a short list or a spoken summary. It names content, never a screen shape. Left out: description, price, then the fields of type place, of those the market has.

items.description: The name of one of the market's listing fields; build/check.sh checks that it is.

review.description: The fields a review here holds besides the ones every review holds (subject, score, text and listing), by name. A review may leave out any of them, and every shared one but subject. Left out: none.

word.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters.

line.description: One line of text that is not only spaces.

role.description: The role's word, the second half of its labels.

listings.description: What this role's listings are: offers or requests.

fields.description: Fields by name. A name is a key in an entry's body: a lowercase letter, then letters and digits, at most 64 characters, and never files, which the standard keeps for the files an entry names.

type.description: One of the nine types in build/types.json.

description.description: What the field holds, in one line.

values.description: For a choice: the values to choose from.

labels.description: For a choice: how people read a value whose words are wrong, such as XL for xl. A value's words are the value with hyphens as spaces and a capital first letter. Each key is one of the field's values; build/check.sh checks that it is. Left out: every value reads as its words.

per.description: For a money field: what its amount may be for, such as hour or session. An amount may always leave per out, for the whole deal. Left out: it always does.

radiusKm.description: For a place field, and always on one: the radius, in whole kilometres, a new place starts at before the person changes it. A place may hold any whole radius.

unit.description: For a number field, and always on one: what the number counts or measures, from one shared list, so an app or an AI can show and convert it without reading the description. build/README.md says what each one measures.

range.description: For a number field: it may hold a range, { from, to }, instead of one number, such as ages from 9 to 11; either end may be left out, for no limit that way, as from 18 alone is 18 and over. One number still fits. Never with many. Left out: one number only.

many.description: The field holds a list of its type, each item different, such as ["weekly", "monthly"] for a choice, even for one item. Never for words, which is a list already, nor with range. Left out otherwise.

roles.description: The market's roles the field is for: in listing, the roles whose listings hold it; in review, the roles of the profile the review is about. Left out: every role.

when.description: The field applies only when each choice field named holds one of the values listed; for a many field, any of its values counts. It names choice fields of the same entry and their values; build/check.sh checks that it does. Left out: always.
